📚 Today you learned

Support and Resistance as Self-Fulfilling Levels

Support and resistance aren't physics — they're consensus. A level matters because enough market participants (algos, fund desks, retail) have orders clustered there, not because of some inherent floor or ceiling in the stock. That's why they work until they don't: once enough size trades through a level, the "support" becomes the next "resistance" on a retest, because everyone who bought there is now underwater and selling to break even. Your GOOG stop at $333.90 sits just under a $338.30-343.93 zone that's held up multiple times this year — real structure, not an arbitrary number. SPXC's story is the opposite: it just broke a 52-week low ($168.88-172.56) with no base underneath, which is exactly why "it's cheap relative to the old range" is a trap — old support becomes irrelevant once price closes clean through it on volume. When you place a stop, you're betting the crowd defends the level one more time; when it fails anyway (like SPXC), that tells you something changed, not that the level was wrong.

Also today: Breakdown confirmation — a level is only confirmed broken on a closing basis, not an intraday wick; SPXC's repeated new-lows this week are closes, not noise.
